translations.text: And it came to pass, after Israel was carried away captive and Jerusalem was laid waste, that Jeremiah sat weeping and lamented with this lamentation over Jerusalem, and he said:
1. Aleph. How this city that was full of people sits alone! She who was great among the nations has become like a widow; the ruler of the land has become subject to tribute.
2. Beth. She wept bitterly in the night, and her tears were on her cheeks [?]. Among all her lovers there was no one to comfort her. All her friends betrayed her and became her enemies.
3. Gimel. Judah was carried away captive because of her affliction and her great sorrow. She settled among the Gentiles and found no rest. All her pursuers overtook her among her oppressors.
4. Daleth. The roads of Zion mourn, because no one comes to the feast. All her gates are ruined, her priests groan, her virgins are captives, and she herself is in bitterness.
5. He. Her oppressors have become her masters, and her enemies rejoice. God has humbled her because of her many sins against him, and her children have gone into captivity in front of the oppressor.
6. Waw. All her beauty has departed from the daughter of Zion. Her princes have become like rams that find no pasture, and they went on in weakness in front of the pursuer.

7. Zayin. Jerusalem remembered the days of her affliction and her rejection, and all the precious things she had in former days, when her people fell into the hands of the oppressors and there was no one to help her. Her enemies saw her and laughed at her captivity.
8. Heth. Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become a thing tossed about. All who used to praise her despised her, because they saw her shame. She herself sighed and turned away backward.

9. Teth. Her uncleanness is before her feet; she did not remember her end. She has fallen astonishingly, and there is no one to comfort her. Look, O Lord, at my humiliation, for the enemy has made himself great.
10. Yod. The oppressor has stretched out his hand over all her precious things, for she saw the Gentiles enter her sanctuary, the ones you commanded should not enter your congregation.
11. Kaph. All her people sighed as they searched for bread. They gave their precious things for food to keep themselves alive. Look down, O Lord, and see, for I have become despised.

12. Lamed. I say to you, all who pass along the road: turn and see whether there is any pain like my pain, which has come upon me. The Lord has spoken against me and humbled me on the day of his fierce anger.
13. Mem. From on high he sent fire down into my bones and set a net for my feet. He turned me right back. He has given me over to ruin and to grief all day long.

14. Nun. He has kept watch over my sins against him. He crushed me in his hands and made his yoke heavy on my neck. My strength has failed, for the Lord has put pain into my hands, which I cannot withstand.

15. Samekh. The Lord has destroyed all my mighty men in my midst. He has summoned a time against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden the virgin daughter of Judah as in a winepress. For this I weep.
16. Ayin. My eyes have poured down water, for the comforters who might have restored my soul have been taken far from me. My children have been ruined, for the enemy has prevailed.
17. Pe. Zion has stretched out her hands, and there is no one to comfort her. The Lord has commanded that Jacob's oppressors be all around him. Jerusalem has become among them like a woman set apart.
18. Tsade. The Lord is righteous, for I have rebelled against his word. Now hear, all you peoples, and see my pain, for my maidens and my young men have gone into captivity.
19. Qoph. I called to my lovers, but they despised me. My priests and my elders perished in the city, for they were seeking food for themselves to restore their souls, and they found none.

20. Resh. See, O Lord, how I am in distress. My belly is in turmoil, and my heart is turned over within me, for you have made me bitter with bitterness. Outside, the sword has made me childless; inside the house it is like death.

21. Shin. Hear now, for I am groaning, and there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble and rejoiced, because you have done this. You have brought the day upon me, you have called the appointed time, and they have become to me [?] "woe is me, woe is me."
22. Tav. Let all their wickedness come before your face, and glean them as you have gleaned me for all my sins, for my sighs are many and my heart is troubled.
23. Aleph. How the Lord in his wrath has darkened the daughter of Zion! He has cast the glory of Israel down from heaven to earth, and has not remembered his footstool on the day of his wrath.

24. Beth. The Lord has swallowed up all the beauty of Jacob without mercy. In his anger he has torn down the strongholds of the daughter of Judah and brought them to the ground. He has defiled her kings and her princes.

25. Gimel. In the wrath of his anger he has broken every horn of Israel. He has turned back from before the enemy, and he has kindled a consuming fire in Jacob, and it has devoured everything around him.

26. Daleth. He has bent his bow like an enemy and made his right hand strong like an attacker. He has slain everything my heart desired in the dwelling of the daughter of Zion. He has poured out his anger like fire.

27. He. The Lord has become like an enemy to me. He has torn down Jerusalem and swallowed up all her palaces. He has destroyed all her strength, and he has multiplied the humbled and fallen among all the daughters of Judah.

28. Vav. He has stripped his tabernacle bare like a vineyard and has done away with his feasts. The Lord has made Zion forget feasts and sabbaths, and in the fury of his anger he has provoked king, priest and prince.

29. Zayin. The Lord has cast away his altar and scattered his sanctuary. By the hand of the enemies he has broken down the wall of her palaces. He raised a cry of battle in the house of the Lord, like the singing of the Levites on a feast day.

30. Heth. The Lord set his heart on destroying the walls of the daughter of Zion. He stretched out the measuring line and did not draw back his hand from casting down. The rampart mourned, and the wall grew weak along with it.

31. Teth. Her gates have sunk into the depths below. Her bars were destroyed and broken. Her king and her princes are among the nations. There is no law, and her prophets have seen no vision from the Lord.

32. Yod. The elders of the daughter of Zion sat on the ground and fell silent. They cast dust on their heads and girded themselves with sackcloth. The leaders of the virgin daughter of Jerusalem were brought down to the ground.

33. Kaph. My eyes have failed with tears. My belly is troubled. My glory has been poured out on the earth over the destruction of the daughter of my people, as nursing infants faint in the streets of the city.
34. Lamed. They said to their mothers, "Where is the wheat and the wine?" as they fainted like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their souls were poured out in their mothers' bosoms.

35. Mem. What shall I testify to you, or to what shall I liken you, O daughter of Jerusalem? Who will save you, or who will comfort you, O virgin daughter of Zion? For the cup of your destruction has grown great. Who will heal you?
36. Nun. Your prophets saw your vanity and folly. They revealed your iniquity so that your captivity might be turned back. They saw for you a parable of vanity, and they drove you out.

37. Samekh. All who pass along the road clapped their hands. They hissed and shook their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city of which they said, 'A crown of glory, a fair beauty, the joy of all the earth'?"

38. Ayin. The Lord has done what he willed. He has fulfilled his word, which he commanded from the days of old. He has overthrown and has not spared. He has made the enemy rejoice over you and has raised up the horn of your oppressors.

39. Pe. All your enemies opened their mouths against you. They hissed and gnashed their teeth and said, "Let us swallow her up, for this is the day we were waiting for. We have found it and have seen it."
40. Tsade. Their heart cried out to the Lord. O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like torrents day and night. Give yourself no rest, and do not let the pupils of your eyes be still.

41. Qoph. Arise at night and exercise yourself [?] at the beginning of your watch. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands for your infant daughters, who are faint with hunger at the head of every street.

42. Resh. Look, O Lord, and look down: whom have you gleaned like this? Shall women eat the fruit of their womb? The cook has made a gleaning, and the nursing infants have been slain. Shall priest and prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?

43. Shin. Children and old men lay down to sleep at the openings of the road. My virgins and my young men went into captivity. You slew them in the day of your wrath. You butchered them and did not spare.

44. Tav. You summoned my communities round about as if to a feast day, and no one escaped on the day of the Lord's wrath. Those who remained I nurtured, strengthened and multiplied, and my enemy has destroyed them all.
45. Aleph. I am the man who has seen poverty under the rod of his wrath. He took me and led me into darkness and not into light. For he turned his hand against me and changed it all day long.
46. Beth. He has wasted my flesh and my skin, and broken my bones. He has built a wall against me and surrounded me. He has wearied my head, and set me in darkness like those long dead.

47. Gimel. He has walled me in, and I cannot get out; he has made the yoke on my neck heavy. Even when I cried out and shouted, my prayer was shut out. He blocked my ways with marble, and a bear lying in wait ruined my paths.

48. Daleth. He became to me one who lies in wait. Like a lion from its hiding place he hunted me when I was set apart. He overtook me, tore me to pieces and ruined me. He bent his bow and filled me with arrows like a target [?].

49. He. He weighed out [?] the venom of his quivers into my kidneys. I became a laughingstock to all the people, a thing for them to make sport of all day long. He filled me with bitterness and made me drunk with sorrow.
50. Vav. He broke my teeth with stone and fed me ashes. He drove my soul away from peace, and I forgot what is good. I said: my victory and my hope come from the Lord.
51. Zayin. I remembered my poverty and my persecution, my bitterness and my grief. I remembered these things well, and my soul fainted within me. I laid this to heart, and therefore I hope in him.

52. Heth. The mercies of the Lord are many and have not failed, for his compassions have not come to an end. He renews them like the dawn in the morning. Your faithfulness has grown great in the morning. My sighs are many, and my heart has failed. "The Lord is my portion," said my soul, "therefore I will wait for him."

53. Teth. The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him. It is good to wait patiently and to hope for the salvation of the Lord. It is good for a man to take up a heavy yoke from his youth. Let him sit alone and be silent, for he has taken up a heavy yoke in his youth.
54. Yod. Let him put his mouth in the dust, if there is hope in enduring. Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him, and be filled with insults.

55. Kaph. For the Lord will not cast off forever. The one who brought low will himself show mercy, according to his great mercy. For he did not speak and bring low with all his heart, nor did he cast away the children of men.
56 [?]. Lamed. To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth, to twist a man's justice before the face of the Most High, to condemn a man in his own cause: the Lord did not say this.
57. Mem. Who spoke thus, and it came to be? The Lord did not command it. Do not evil and good come from the mouth of the Lord? Why does a living man complain, a man about his own sins?

58. Nun. He has searched out our way and examined it. Let us return to the Lord. Let us lift up our hearts with our hands and look to the Most High, who dwells in the heavens. We have sinned and acted godlessly, and you have not pardoned.

59. Samekh. You have covered us in anger and pursued us. You have slain us and not spared. You spread a thick cloud over yourself, so that our prayer would not reach you. You have made us a byword and a mockery among the peoples.

60. Ayin. Our eyes are in grief and will not cease; let there be no relief, until he looks down from heaven and takes notice. My eyes have failed, together with my soul, over the daughters of my people.
61. Pe. All our enemies opened their mouths against me over the ruin of my people.
62. Tsade. My enemies hunted me down like a sparrow, without cause. They put my life to death in the pit; they laid a stone upon me. Water flowed over my head, and I said, "I am cast off."
63. Qoph. I called on your name, O Lord, from the lowest pit; you heard my voice. Do not make your ears heavy to my cry. Draw near on the day when I called on you, and you said to me, "Do not fear."
64. Resh. You have judged the cases of my soul, O Lord, and redeemed my life. You have seen my troubles, O Lord; judge my cause. You have seen all their vengeance and all their schemes against me.

65. Shin. You have heard their reproach, O Lord, and all their words against me. The [?] of their lips and their schemes against me go on all day long. Look at their sitting down and their rising up, for I have become their byword.

66. Tav. Give them their recompense, O Lord, the snare of their heart, according to the works of their hands. Give them the help of my heart; let toil be theirs. Pursue them in your wrath, O Lord, and destroy them under the heavens.
67. Aleph. How the gold has grown dark! The fine silver has been changed. The [?] stones are scattered at the head of every street.
68. Beth. The sons of Zion, prized above gold, how they are reckoned as earthen vessels made by the potter's hand!
69. Gimel. Even sea monsters bare their breasts and suckle their young, but the daughters of my people have become incurable, like sparrows in the wilderness.
70. Daleth. Their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth from thirst. The infants [?] asked for bread, and there was no one to break it for them.
71. He. Those who ate luxurious food perished in the streets. Those raised on purple were defiled with dung.
72. Vav. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people became greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown with an everlasting overthrow, and no one [?] hands in her.
73. Zayin. Her devout ones were purer than snow and whiter than milk, and their colour was redder than sapphire stone.
74. Heth. Their appearance became blacker than coal; they were not recognised in the streets. Their skin clung to their bones; they withered and were broken like firewood.
75. Teth. Those wounded by the sword were better off than those wounded by famine. I grieve over those [?] from the fruits of the trees of the grove.
76. Yod. With the hands of compassionate women their children were cooked. They became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
77. Kaph. The Lord gave full vent to his fury and poured out his wrath. He kindled a fire in Zion, and it devoured her foundations.
78. Lamed. The kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world did not believe that an enemy and oppressor would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
79. Mem. It was because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed righteous blood.
80. Nun. Her young men fell in her streets. They were defiled with blood; in their weakness they were consumed together with their garments.

81. Samekh. "Get away from the unclean, you unclean!" they said to us. "Get away from the unclean, get away, and do not touch them, for they have provoked anger." Say among the nations: "You shall no longer continue to dwell as strangers before the face of the Lord."
82. Ayin. Our eyes failed as we looked for our help, as we watched in vain, for we were looking to a nation that could not save us.
83. Pe. The face of the Lord is their portion; he will not look upon them again, for they showed no respect to the priests, and had no mercy on the elders.
84. Tsade. They hunted our little ones so that they could not go into our streets. Our footprints disappeared, and our time drew near: our days were ended, our [?] has come.
85. Qoph. Our pursuers are swifter than the eagles of the sky. On the mountains they [?], and in the desert they lay in wait for us.
86. Resh. The breath of our face, Christ the Lord, was caught in their destructions, he of whom we said: "Under his shadow we will live among the nations."
87. Shin. Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who live in the land of Uz, for the cup of the Lord will come to you too: you will drink it, get drunk, and vomit.
88. Tav. Your iniquity has come to an end, daughter of Zion; he will not carry you away into captivity again. I will punish your iniquities, daughter of Zion; your ungodly deeds have been revealed...
Remember, O Lord, what has happened to us. Look down and see our disgrace.
Our houses have gone to others, to strangers.
We have become orphans, like people who have no father. Our mothers have become like widows.
We drank our own water for money, the water that was ours in our earlier days. We got our own wood for a price, carrying it on our backs.
We were persecuted and grew weary, and we could find no rest.
Egypt gave a hand to Assyria so that they could be filled.
Our fathers sinned and are no more, and their iniquities have been heaped on us.
Slaves have ruled over us, and there is no one to rescue us from their hand.
We will get our bread at the risk of our lives, in the face of the sword of the [?].
Our skin turned black like an oven; it shrivelled before the scorching wind of famine.
They humbled the women in Zion and defiled the virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes were hanged by their hands, and they showed no honour to the faces of the elders.
The chosen young men ground meal, and the youths were crucified on the wood.
The effeminate [?] were gone from the gates, and the chosen young men stopped their singing.
And the joy of our heart was broken; our dancing [?] was turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned.
Because of this our heart has become sick with grief; because of this our eyes have grown dark.
Upon Mount Zion, for it has been destroyed, and foxes walked about in it.
But you, Lord, are forever, and your throne is from generation to generation.
Why do you utterly forget us, and forsake us for length of days?
Turn us back to yourself, Lord, and we shall turn back; and renew our days as they were at first.
For you have cast us out and put us far from you, and you have been exceedingly angry with us.
